_what: Referee-authored GOLD for the litkb P5 bulk pass and the operational fix set. Eight extracted files chosen by a seeded draw, one page each, hand-annotated from the RENDERED page image only (pypdfium2 render scale 2.0, read as PNG); plus twenty equation blocks chosen by a second seeded draw, each read from a rendered crop of its own bbox. Committed BEFORE any block text, any stored LaTeX, any table row and any reconcile output was read (CLAUDE.md 3.4c).
_not_consulted: What WAS read to build this file: litkb.main_files metadata only (rel_path, pages, sha256, current_run_id IS NOT NULL) to define the population; litkb.blocks/litkb.equations METADATA only for the equation draw (block id, rel_path, page_no, bbox, under the predicate latex IS NOT NULL — the predicate, never the value); the blocks_type_check CHECK constraint, to spell kinds in the pipeline's own vocabulary; and the source of inventory.page_frames / docling.to_canonical / docling.to_mediabox, to map a canonical bbox onto a rendered page. What was NOT read: blocks.text, blocks.type, blocks.reading_order, equations.latex, litkb.tables, litkb.table_cells, extraction_runs.metrics, any reconcile() output, any litkb_search result, and every number in Reports/LITKB_P5_BULK_2026-09-16.md that could have steered a reading.
_frame: Reading order is the order a HUMAN reads the page: single column top-to-bottom; two-column left column fully, then right column; a full-width element is read in the band where it sits (a full-width table above the columns is read before both columns, one below them after both). Furniture (running head, page number, banner, footer, side stamp, publisher badge) is recorded but excluded from the body order.
_kinds: The 18 values of litkb.blocks.blocks_type_check: title | author | affiliation | abstract | heading | paragraph | list_item | footnote | caption | table | figure | equation | reference | page_header | page_footer | page_number | sidebar | other. A gold item may name an ACCEPTABLE SET (kind_any) where two of those words describe the same object equally well (e.g. an abstract paragraph is 'abstract' or 'paragraph'; a Nature title-page affiliation footer is 'affiliation' or 'footnote'); scoring counts a live kind inside the set as correct and says which was used.
_snippet_rule: Each body snippet is the first ~5-10 words of the block AS PRINTED, with no hyphenation repair. A scorer matches it whitespace-normalised and case-insensitively into a canonical block's text.

_scoring.reading_order: For each ordered PAIR of gold body items matched to live canonical blocks, the pair is a VIOLATION when the live reading_order inverts the gold order. Report two counts separately: (a) within-column / within-band inversions — a real violation; (b) cross-column or cross-band inversions — the layout is genuinely ambiguous for a machine (a column-major reader and a band-major reader disagree), so these are reported and NOT charged as defects unless the live order is inconsistent with BOTH readings.
_scoring.kind: A gold item scores CORRECT when the matched live block's type equals the gold kind, or is in kind_any where given. Score kind accuracy per page as correct / matched.
_scoring.text_equality: TWO grades, both reported. STRICT: the gold verbatim_paragraph equals the live block text byte for byte after UTF-8 encoding. OPERATING: equal after (1) CRLF and LF collapsed to a single space, (2) runs of whitespace collapsed to one space, (3) a hyphen at a line break joined ("can-\nopy" -> "canopy"), (4) Unicode punctuation folded to ASCII (U+2018/U+2019 -> ', U+201C/U+201D -> \", U+2013/U+2014 -> -, U+00A0 -> space), (5) leading/trailing space stripped. The referee expects STRICT to fail on most pages and says so in advance: the P8 referee proved (LITKB_OPERATIONAL_REFEREE_2026-09-16.md 2.1) that stored blocks keep line breaks and that extractors de-hyphenate and substitute glyphs. STRICT failing is therefore NOT a defect on its own; OPERATING failing IS one, and the diff is reported either way. A gold paragraph that the live extraction SPLIT across more than one block is reported as 'split-N', and the operating grade is then run against the concatenation of the covering blocks in reading order.
_scoring.table_rows: DATA rows only: every row printed inside the table's ruled frame that is not a column-header row. Rows printed OUTSIDE the frame, and floating annotation cells, are named separately and not counted. Header rows are given as a separate count. A live table whose row count equals the gold data-row count, or that count plus the header count, is graded MATCH with the convention named; anything else is a MISS.
_scoring.equation_latex: Three grades. IDENTICAL: the stored LaTeX renders the same expression with the same tokens as the referee's reading. EQUIVALENT: the same mathematics, differing only in spelling that a LaTeX renderer treats alike (\frac vs \dfrac, \mathbb{R} vs \mathbb R, ( ) vs \left( \right), a missing or extra equation NUMBER, \text{} vs \mathrm{}, whitespace, or an alignment environment choice). WRONG: a different symbol, a dropped or added term, a wrong index or limit, a truncated expression, or content from outside the box. UNSTABLE: the crop itself does not determine the answer (a glyph the render cannot resolve), which is graded separately and never counted as WRONG.
_scoring.presence: For each gold page, every body item must be covered by at least one canonical block of the CURRENT run; an uncovered item is a MISS and is listed.

files.procedure: population = litkb.main_files WHERE status='active' AND current_run_id IS NOT NULL, sorted by rel_path; random.Random(seed).sample(rows, 8); then for each file page = rng.randint(1, pages) drawn from the SAME stream in pick order.
files.population_sha256_of: sha256 of the newline-joined sorted rel_path list

equations.procedure: population = litkb.equations e JOIN litkb.blocks b JOIN litkb.main_files f ON f.current_run_id=b.run_id WHERE e.latex IS NOT NULL AND f.status='active', sorted by block id; random.Random(seed).sample(rows, 20).
equations.population_sha256_of: sha256 of the newline-joined sorted block_id list
equations.render: page rendered at scale 3.0; the canonical bbox is TOP-LEFT in the MEDIABOX frame, so the drawn rectangle is (x-dx, y-dy)*3.0 with (dx,dy) from inventory.page_frames; 14 pt of context kept around it so a frame error would show as a displaced rectangle rather than a silent mis-read.

verbatim_paragraph.text: While there are strengths associated with this methodology, there are also many limitations. As identified through descriptive coding, issues associated with image obstruction and quality resulted in the inability to assess tree presence/absence for hundreds of trees. Existing studies that have used aerial imagery to assess tree retention have used images with resolutions ranging from 15 cm to 1 m to confidently classify survival status of trees between 5 and 20 years old (Ko et al. 2015a, 2015b). The difference in success classifying trees at different image resolutions could be due to differences in canopy cover and other vegetation presences between Toronto, Ontario, and Sacramento, California, USA, the focus of Ko et al.'s (2015a, 2015b) studies. While those studies were supplemented with 2 field visits, which also could have helped increase confidence in classification between visit years, we found that even with image resolution of 8 cm, it can be difficult to assess retention, particularly for trees under 5 years old in yards that include other vegetation and building shadows.

Comparing the quarterly map results for NDVIorg-only (Figure 7A-D) and HVHHmt-only revealed that changes are flagged much earlier due to the dense observation density of NDVIorg, but often are confirmed later.

For Wetland, the most common disagreement was with Tree Cover (56%), and for Developed the two most common classes of disagreement were Grass/Shrub (36%) and Tree Cover (34%). Barren class disagreement was almost exclusively with Grass/Shrub and found in the arid and semi-arid areas of the West reporting region.

body_order.snippet: Spatial validation reveals poor predictive performance of large-scale ecological mapping models
Pierre Ploton 1, Frédéric Mortier 2,3, Maxime Réjou-Méchain1
Mapping aboveground forest biomass is central for assessing the global carbon balance
1 AMAP, Univ Montpellier, IRD, CNRS, INRAE, CIRAD, Montpellier, France.

verbatim_paragraph.text: Mapping aboveground forest biomass is central for assessing the global carbon balance. However, current large-scale maps show strong disparities, despite good validation statistics of their underlying models. Here, we attribute this contradiction to a flaw in the validation methods, which ignore spatial autocorrelation (SAC) in data, leading to overoptimistic assessment of model predictive power. To illustrate this issue, we reproduce the approach of large-scale mapping studies using a massive forest inventory dataset of 11.8 million trees in central Africa to train and validate a random forest model based on multispectral and environmental variables. A standard nonspatial validation method suggests that the model predicts more than half of the forest biomass variation, while spatial validation methods accounting for SAC reveal quasi-null predictive power. This study underscores how a common practice in big data mapping studies shows an apparent high predictive power, even when predictors have poor relationships with the ecological variable of interest, thus possibly leading to erroneous maps and interpretations.
